_comment: availability_from and availability_to are shifted forward by whole weeks at load time, relative to dates_anchored_to (shift_availability in api/mock_travel.py); merchant_occupancy.json shifts the same way. Author the dates as if dates_anchored_to were today.

products.title: ACME Guesthouses Alfama
products.short_description: An eight-room townhouse folded into Alfama's stairstep lanes, with azulejo-lined hallways and breakfast under a lemon tree.
products.long_description: ACME Guesthouses occupies a restored 18th-century townhouse a two-minute walk from the miradouro viewpoints of old Lisbon. Rooms keep the original beamed ceilings and tile work, and breakfast is served in the lemon-tree courtyard until a civilized 11am. The published price is an advance-saver rate — non-refundable, which is how eight rooms this loved stay under the neighborhood's going rate. Expect steep lanes and church bells rather than car traffic — that is the point.

specs.view: Alfama rooftops with a sliver of river

review_highlights: The courtyard breakfast alone is worth the rate — fresh pastries and that lemon tree
Perfect base for wandering; we never once needed a taxi
Pack light: it's gorgeous but there are stairs everywhere and no lift

products.title: ACME Hotels Lisbon Riverside
products.short_description: A polished riverfront hotel with a rooftop infinity pool aimed straight at the Tagus and the evening ferry lights.
products.long_description: The Lisbon flagship of ACME Hotels sits where the city meets the river, five minutes on foot from the food halls and night-time energy of Cais do Sodre. Floor-to-ceiling windows, a serious cocktail bar, and a rooftop pool that stays open until midnight make it the splurge-night pick. Breakfast is a la carte downstairs rather than included, and worth ordering the custard-filled everything.
review_highlights: Sunset from the rooftop pool is the best free show in Lisbon
Beds are absurdly comfortable; blackout blinds actually black out
Skip the in-house breakfast and hit the market next door

products.title: ACME Guesthouses Baixa
products.short_description: A friendly, no-frills guesthouse on a pedestrian Baixa street — small rooms, big location, honest price.
products.long_description: ACME Guesthouses keeps it simple: clean compact doubles above a tiled stairwell, a help-yourself espresso machine on the landing, and the entire flat grid of downtown Lisbon outside the front door. Rooms facing the street get the buskers until about 10pm; rooms at the back get the quiet. At this price in this postcode, it books out fast.

specs.view: pedestrian street or interior light well
specs.wifi: free, can be patchy on upper floors

review_highlights: Unbeatable location for the money — everything is walkable
Room was small but spotless, exactly as photographed
Ask for a back room if you're a light sleeper

products.title: ACME Suites Graca Rooftop
products.short_description: Six rooftop suites in hilltop Graca, each with a private terrace looking over the whole amphitheater of Lisbon.
products.long_description: ACME Suites converted the top floors of a Graca corner building into suites that feel like small apartments, each with its own terrace, espresso setup, and a panorama from castle to river. Breakfast arrives in a basket at your door at the time you choose. The hill keeps casual foot traffic away — the famous tram stop is around the corner when your legs surrender.

specs.view: full city panorama from private terrace

review_highlights: Drinking morning coffee above the entire city — unreal
Breakfast basket at 7:30 sharp every day, still-warm bread
It's a real hill; embrace the tram

products.title: ACME Ryokan Gion
products.short_description: A hushed tatami ryokan behind a noren curtain in Gion, with a private moss garden and a cypress soaking tub.
products.long_description: ACME Ryokan hides eight tatami suites down a lantern-lit lane in the heart of Gion. Evenings end with a soak in the hinoki cypress tub overlooking your own pocket of moss garden; mornings start with a multi-dish Japanese breakfast served in-room at the hour you choose. Staff speak English and will book seasonal tea ceremonies and dinner counters before they fill.
review_highlights: The breakfast tray was the most beautiful meal of our trip
Silent at night in a way that feels impossible for a city
Futons are firm by design — ask for the extra topper if unsure

products.title: ACME Ryokan Arashiyama Riverside
products.short_description: A riverside ryokan-style inn at the foot of Arashiyama's maple slopes — the autumn-foliage address in Kyoto.
products.long_description: ACME Ryokan sits directly on the Katsura riverbank, where November turns the facing hillside into a wall of red and gold. Twin rooms open onto the water, breakfast is served overlooking the river, and the bamboo grove is a ten-minute walk before the day-trip crowds arrive. Foliage-season dates sell out months ahead; the inn releases its full calendar each spring.
review_highlights: Watched the mist lift off the river from bed — worth every yen
Go early to the grove like the staff tell you to; they're right
Book the moment dates open, seriously

products.title: ACME Hotels Kyoto Station Garden Hotel
products.short_description: A calm, efficient hotel wrapped around an interior garden, three minutes from Kyoto Station's rail lines.
products.long_description: The Kyoto property of ACME Hotels trades old-town atmosphere for logistics: every major rail line, airport train, and day-trip platform is a short covered walk away. Rooms are compact, immaculate, and face a surprisingly serene interior garden courtyard rather than the street. The non-refundable rate keeps it well under comparable station hotels.
review_highlights: Ideal day-trip base — we did three regions in three days
Quietest station-adjacent hotel I've ever stayed in
Rooms are tight; fine for two organized people

products.title: ACME Ryokan Higashiyama Annex
products.short_description: A whole restored machiya townhouse to yourselves on a lantern-lit Higashiyama lane, sleeping four.
products.long_description: The Annex is a single two-storey machiya — private entrance, hinoki bath, small kitchen, and a tsubo garden you can see from the soaking tub. A breakfast chef arrives each morning unless you wave them off, and the temple paths of Higashiyama begin at the end of the lane. It is the priciest key ACME Ryokan offers and routinely the best-reviewed.
review_highlights: Felt like living in Kyoto, not visiting it
The morning chef quietly became the highlight of the trip
Steep machiya stairs — mind them after sake

products.title: ACME Hotels Roma Norte Hotel
products.short_description: A plant-filled Roma Norte hotel with juliet balconies over the cafes and a mezcal-leaning rooftop bar.
products.long_description: ACME Hotels Roma Norte puts you on a leafy block where the city's best coffee, taquerias, and bookshops are all within a five-minute radius. King rooms open onto small balconies above the street; the rooftop bar pours an education in mezcal until 1am. No breakfast service — by design, since the neighborhood does it better.
review_highlights: Stumbling distance from a dozen world-class breakfasts
Rooftop at golden hour is a scene in the best way
Street-facing rooms hear the city wake up — earplugs provided

products.title: ACME Guesthouses Condesa
products.short_description: The Condesa outpost of ACME Guesthouses: ten rooms around a fern-filled courtyard, two blocks from the park loop.
products.long_description: The Mexico City sibling of the Lisbon original keeps the same formula — a historic house, a green courtyard at its heart, and breakfast that ends when you say it ends. Garden kings open directly onto the ferns; upstairs rooms get more light and a shared terrace. Avenida Amsterdam's running loop and the dog-watching benches of Condesa are around the corner.
review_highlights: Chilaquiles at breakfast, every day, zero regrets
The courtyard is a cool, quiet pocket in a buzzing neighborhood
Upstairs rooms are brighter if you want morning sun

products.title: ACME Hotels Centro Hotel
products.short_description: A dependable, great-value hotel one street off the Zocalo, with a hot breakfast buffet included.
products.long_description: ACME Hotels is the workhorse pick for first-time visitors who want the historic center outside the lobby door. Rooms are simple and well kept, the included breakfast buffet runs to fresh fruit, eggs to order, and pan dulce, and the cathedral bells are your alarm clock. The non-refundable rate is among the lowest reliable beds in the Centro.
review_highlights: Location is everything — we walked to all the big sights
Breakfast was far better than the price suggested
It's the Centro: lively until late, bring earplugs

products.title: ACME Hotels Polanco Skyline Suites
products.short_description: Glassy corner suites above Polanco with wraparound views over the Chapultepec treetops.
products.long_description: The Polanco tower of ACME Hotels is the business-and-anniversaries property: corner suites with two walls of glass, a 25-meter lap pool, and the museums and tasting menus of Polanco within walking distance. Park-facing suites look across the green sweep of Chapultepec to the skyline beyond. Sofa beds make it the practical pick for a trio.
review_highlights: That corner view at dusk is worth the upgrade alone
Quiet, polished, runs like a watch
More formal in feel than Roma — pick your vibe

products.title: ACME Stays Harbourfront Lofts
products.short_description: Warm timber lofts on Reykjavik's old harbour, with full kitchens and whale-boat masts outside the window.
products.long_description: ACME Stays converted a harbourfront warehouse into split-level lofts that sleep four without anyone touching a sofa cushion at 2am — the queen sits upstairs under the skylight. Full kitchens earn their keep in a city where dinner out adds up, and the harbour walk into town takes eight minutes. In winter months the skylight doubles as a lazy person's aurora alarm.
review_highlights: Cooked half our meals and saved a fortune
Saw the lights from the skylight in November, half asleep
Harbour gulls start early — part of the charm, mostly

products.title: ACME Lodges Laugavegur Hotel
products.short_description: A snug Nordic hotel right on the main shopping street, with a famously good included breakfast.
products.long_description: The Laugavegur house of ACME Lodges is the sensible heart-of-town option: wool throws, blackout curtains tuned for bright June nights, and a ground-floor breakfast of skyr, rye, smoked fish, and waffles that guests plan their mornings around. Tour pickups stop at the corner. The non-refundable rate undercuts most of the street.
review_highlights: Breakfast waffles deserve their reputation
Couldn't be better placed for shops and bars
Front rooms hear the weekend runtur — ask for the back

products.title: ACME Stays Old Town Townhouse
products.short_description: A corrugated-iron heritage townhouse in the old quarter — two bedrooms, a wood stove, and breakfast delivered.
products.long_description: This is the flagship of ACME Stays: a candy-red 1906 townhouse on a quiet old-town corner, restored with sheep-wool insulation and a working wood stove in the sitting room. Two proper bedrooms and a sofa bed make it the family-or-friends pick, and a breakfast crate from the bakery two doors down lands on the doorstep each morning. The pond, parliament square, and the city's best hot dogs are all within four minutes on foot.
review_highlights: Like borrowing a stylish friend's house for the week
Wood stove + storm outside = peak Iceland evening
Book early; there's exactly one of it

products.title: ACME Lodges Fjordview Cabins

attributes.neighborhood: fjord edge, 25 min drive from center

products.short_description: Architect-designed cabins on a dark fjord shore, each with a private outdoor hot tub under the northern sky.
products.long_description: Twenty-five minutes from downtown Reykjavik, the Fjordview cabins trade walkability for silence, sea, and zero light pollution. Each cabin pairs a glass gable facing the water with a private geothermal hot tub on the deck — the September-to-December aurora season is the reason most guests come. A car is essential; a grocery stop on the way out is strongly advised.
review_highlights: Aurora directly overhead from the hot tub — I will never recover
Total silence except the water; slept like the dead
You need a car and groceries, plan for both

products.title: ACME Riads Medina Courtyard
products.short_description: A six-room riad deep in the medina, built around a zellige-tiled courtyard with a trickling fountain.
products.long_description: ACME Riads is the classic medina experience at an honest price: a carved cedar door on an unmarked derb, then a cool tiled courtyard, orange trees, and six rooms over two floors. Breakfast — msemen, amlou, fresh juice, endless mint tea — is served on the roof terrace with the Koutoubia minaret on the horizon. Staff will walk you to the souk entrance until the lanes start making sense.

specs.extras: roof terrace, hammam bookings, airport transfer on request

review_highlights: The courtyard is ten degrees cooler than the souk — pure relief
Breakfast on the roof at sunrise, call to prayer drifting over
Let them walk you home the first night; the derbs are a maze

products.title: ACME Riads & Hammam
products.short_description: An indulgent riad with its own candlelit hammam, a plunge pool, and Atlas views from the roof terrace.
products.long_description: ACME Riads is the riad you book to be looked after: suites with hand-painted ceilings, a courtyard plunge pool, and a private in-house hammam where the traditional scrub is half the reason guests rebook. The roof terrace serves breakfast and sunset drinks with the High Atlas floating behind the medina skyline. Quiet by riad standards, being a few lanes off the main souk arteries.

specs.hammam: private, on site, bookable by the hour

review_highlights: The hammam scrub left me a new person
Staff anticipated everything — taxis, tables, a birthday cake we never mentioned twice
Splurge on the terrace dinner at least once

products.title: ACME Hotels Marrakesh Palm Grove Resort
products.short_description: A palm-grove resort outside the medina walls — three pools, garden pavilions, and a free shuttle into the souk.
products.long_description: The Palm Grove resort of ACME Hotels is the decompression option: low pavilion rooms scattered through a working palm grove, three pools at different temperatures, and dinner under the palms with the medina a 20-minute shuttle away. Garden pavilions sleep three and open onto private patios. December holiday weeks sell out far in advance.
review_highlights: Two days in the souk, one day by the pool — the correct rhythm
Pavilion patios are blissfully private
The shuttle runs hourly; screenshot the timetable

products.title: ACME Lodges Lakefront Lodge
products.short_description: A timber-and-stone lodge on the Lake Wakatipu shore, five minutes' walk from town and the gondola base.
products.long_description: The flagship lodge of ACME Lodges fronts directly onto the lake, with king rooms angled so the first thing you see each morning is water and the saw-toothed ranges behind it. The included breakfast leans hearty for ski-season appetites — July through September guests get a drying room and a waxing bench in the basement. Town's restaurants are a flat five-minute lakeside stroll.
review_highlights: Opened the curtains and actually gasped
Perfect ski base — drying room, big breakfast, early shuttle stop outside
Lakeview rooms are worth the difference over courtyard ones

products.title: ACME Retreats Alpine Chalets
products.short_description: Private chalets on the Fernhill ridge with wood fires, full kitchens, and a hundred-kilometer view down the lake.
products.long_description: ACME is four chalets on a steep ridge above town, each with a wood-burning fire, a serious kitchen, and a deck cantilevered toward the longest view in Queenstown. Sleeping four across a king and two singles, they suit families and ski groups who want to self-cater and come home to silence. Five minutes' drive to town; the alpine parrots do occasionally inspect the deck railings.

specs.view: length of Lake Wakatipu and the snowline

review_highlights: Fire going, snow falling, that view — didn't want to leave the chalet
Kitchen is genuinely well equipped, not hotel-pretend
You'll want a car for the hill

products.title: ACME Lodges Lakefront Studios
products.short_description: Compact self-contained studios in the middle of town — kitchenette, laundry, and every trailhead shuttle nearby.
products.long_description: The in-town studios of ACME Lodges are built for travelers who treat the room as a basecamp: kitchenette, gear storage, guest laundry, and the bus exchange, supermarkets, and burger queues of central Queenstown within two blocks. Rooms face an interior courtyard, which keeps Friday nights surprisingly quiet. The non-refundable rate is the cheapest reliable bed this close to the center.
review_highlights: Everything you need, nothing you don't, two minutes from everything
Used the kitchenette daily — saved heaps
It's a basecamp, not a honeymoon suite, and that's fine

products.title: New York to Lisbon Nonstop — Economy
products.short_description: ACME Air Atlantic's evening nonstop to Lisbon — leave after work, land with the whole morning ahead.
products.long_description: The 18:40 departure is timed so economy passengers can eat, sleep most of the crossing, and clear Lisbon arrivals before 7am local. Seatback screens, USB-C at every seat, and a light pre-landing breakfast are included; checked bags are not on this fare. As a non-refundable basic fare it is consistently the cheapest way across on this route.

specs.bag_allowance: 1 carry-on + personal item; checked 23 kg bag $35

review_highlights: Slept five hours and walked into Lisbon by 8am — efficient
Newer cabin than expected at this price
Remember the bag fee when comparing fares

products.title: New York to Lisbon Nonstop — Premium Economy
products.short_description: The same overnight Lisbon nonstop with a wider seat, deeper recline, and a fully refundable fare.
products.long_description: ACME Air Atlantic's premium economy cabin sits in its own quiet section of eight rows: 96 cm of pitch, a leg rest that matters on an overnight, and dinner served on actual ceramics. The fare includes two checked bags and full refundability up to 24 hours before departure. The price is roughly double economy; the sleep quality is roughly double too.
review_highlights: Actually slept, actually refundable — earned its price
The small cabin feels semi-private
Window pairs are the move for couples

products.title: Boston to Lisbon Nonstop — Economy
products.short_description: A late-evening Boston departure on the shortest US nonstop to Lisbon, on a flexible refundable fare.
products.long_description: At six and a half hours this is the quickest way from the US East Coast to Portugal, and the 21:15 push-back suits travelers connecting in from elsewhere in New England that evening. The standard economy fare here is fully refundable until 24 hours out and includes one checked bag. Arrival lands you in Lisbon just after 8am.
review_highlights: Shortest hop across the Atlantic I've found
Refundable fare saved us when plans moved by a week
Boarding was calm and on time both directions

products.title: San Francisco to Kyoto — Economy, One Stop
products.short_description: ACME Air Pacific's best-value routing to Kyoto, with a single short connection and rail transfer included.
products.long_description: This itinerary crosses the Pacific on ACME Air Pacific's flagship widebody, connects once at the airline's coastal hub, and includes the express rail transfer into Kyoto Station in the fare. Economy seats have adjustable headrests and free messaging Wi-Fi; meals lean Japanese and are better than the fare class suggests. Non-refundable, but date changes are permitted for a fee.

specs.extras: Kyoto rail transfer included, free messaging Wi-Fi

review_highlights: The included rail transfer removed all arrival stress
Best economy meal I've had over the Pacific
The connection is tight if your first leg runs late

products.title: Los Angeles to Kyoto — Premium Economy, One Stop
products.short_description: A refundable premium-economy crossing to Kyoto with lounge access at the connection and rail transfer included.
products.long_description: ACME Air Pacific's premium economy buys a 38-row-free cabin with 99 cm of pitch, calf rests, and a duvet that survives a trans-Pacific night. The fare is fully refundable, includes two checked bags, lounge access during the hub connection, and the express rail transfer to Kyoto Station. For a fifteen-hour door-to-door day, the difference from economy is substantial.

specs.extras: lounge at connection, Kyoto rail transfer included

review_highlights: Arrived functional after 15 hours, which says everything
Lounge shower at the connection was a reset button
Worth it outbound even if you fly economy home

products.title: Seattle to Kyoto — Economy, One Stop
products.short_description: The Pacific Northwest's flexible route to Kyoto — a morning departure, one easy connection, refundable fare.
products.long_description: Leaving Seattle at 09:50 puts you into Kyoto Station mid-evening the next day with the shortest total travel time from the Northwest. The standard fare is refundable to 24 hours before departure and includes one checked bag and the rail transfer. ACME Air Pacific's daytime Pacific crossings are popular with travelers who prefer staying awake to fighting a red-eye.
review_highlights: Daytime crossing meant zero jet-lag drama for us
Smooth connection, bags made it, transfer worked
Bring a long book — it's a long daylight haul

products.title: Chicago to Mexico City Nonstop — Economy
products.short_description: ACME Air Americas' early nonstop from Chicago — wheels down in Mexico City before lunch.
products.long_description: The 07:20 departure clears you through Mexico City immigration and into a taqueria by early afternoon. ACME Air Americas runs a cheerful single-aisle service on this route: free soft drinks and a snack box, paid Wi-Fi, and a famously punctual operation. The basic fare is non-refundable and carry-on only — add a checked bag at booking for less than at the airport.

specs.bag_allowance: 1 carry-on + personal item; checked 23 kg bag $30

review_highlights: On time both ways, which is all I ask of a 4-hour hop
Landing at 12 means a full first afternoon in the city
Add the bag online — airport price stings

products.title: New York to Mexico City Nonstop — Economy
products.short_description: A refundable morning nonstop from New York, landing in Mexico City in time for a late lunch.
products.long_description: ACME Air Americas' busiest international route runs up to three times daily; this 08:05 rotation is the one regulars book, arriving at 13:35 with the afternoon intact. The standard fare is refundable to 24 hours out and includes a checked bag, which is unusual at this price point. Seats are snug but the flight is short enough not to care.
review_highlights: Refundable AND a free bag at this price — booked twice since
Morning slot dodges the afternoon thunderstorm delays
Middle seats fill fast; pick seats at booking

products.title: Los Angeles to Mexico City Nonstop — Business
products.short_description: ACME Air Americas' evening business cabin to Mexico City — wide cradle seats, a proper dinner, and lounge access.
products.long_description: On the LA evening rotation ACME Air Americas fits its short-haul business product: 2-2 cradle recliners, a plated dinner with Mexican wines, and lounge access before departure. The fare is fully refundable and includes two checked bags and priority everything. At under four hours it is a treat rather than a necessity — which is rather the point.

specs.extras: lounge access, priority boarding and bags

review_highlights: Dinner and a glass of something good, then straight to the hotel
Cradle seats are plenty for a sub-4-hour evening flight
Lounge gets crowded around 5pm — come fed or come early

products.title: New York to Reykjavik Nonstop — Economy
products.short_description: ACME Air North's midnight red-eye to Reykjavik — short, cheap, and you wake up in Iceland.
products.long_description: The 23:30 departure is the classic Iceland play: board, sleep fast, and land at 09:15 with the whole first day ahead. ACME Air North keeps this fare low by unbundling — carry-on is included, checked bags and meals are paid extras, and the fare is non-refundable. At under six hours it is the shortest, cheapest path from the US East Coast to the land of waterfalls.

specs.bag_allowance: 1 carry-on + personal item; checked 20 kg bag $45

review_highlights: Cheapest way to Iceland, and it was perfectly fine
Five hours goes quickly when you board at midnight
Buy the meal or bring one; nothing is free back there

products.title: Boston to Reykjavik Nonstop — Economy
products.short_description: The shortest US nonstop to Reykjavik, on a refundable fare — currently sold out for peak aurora dates.
products.long_description: Boston to Reykjavik is ACME Air North's shortest transatlantic sector, a 5h20m overnight hop that lands at 08:30. This refundable fare includes a checked bag and free changes, which makes it the favorite for aurora-chasers gambling on forecasts — and explains why autumn departures sell out first. ACME Travel will surface alternative dates or the New York departure when this one is full.
review_highlights: Short enough that the red-eye barely hurts
Free changes are gold when you're chasing clear skies
Book months out for September through November

products.title: Chicago to Reykjavik Nonstop — Premium Economy
products.short_description: ACME Air North's small premium cabin from Chicago — wider seats, dinner included, and a refundable fare to Reykjavik.
products.long_description: ACME Air North's premium cabin on the Chicago rotation seats just 22 passengers in 2-2 rows with 94 cm of pitch, an Icelandic dinner service, and two checked bags in the fare. Fully refundable and changeable without fees, it is the comfortable hedge for travelers building an aurora or ring-road trip around uncertain weather. Lands at 09:05, in time to collect a rental car before midday.
review_highlights: Tiny cabin, fast boarding, real food — pleasant surprise
Slept enough to drive the south coast that afternoon
Premium on a 6-hour overnight is a justifiable luxury

products.title: New York to Marrakesh — Economy, One Stop
products.short_description: ACME Air Atlantic's one-stop routing to Marrakesh via its Lisbon hub, with a sub-two-hour connection.
products.long_description: This itinerary rides the evening Lisbon nonstop, then connects onto ACME Air Atlantic's short hop south to Marrakesh, touching down at 12:55 local. The Lisbon connection is 1h50m — enough for a coffee and a leg-stretch without airport sprinting. Non-refundable; one checked bag is included through to Marrakesh.
review_highlights: Connection was painless — same terminal, gates close together
Landed by 1pm and was drinking mint tea in the riad by 3
Overnight leg is the one to sleep on; second hop is short

products.title: Lisbon to Marrakesh Nonstop — Economy
products.short_description: The quick morning hop from Lisbon to Marrakesh — ninety minutes, two continents.
products.long_description: ACME Air Atlantic's mid-morning shuttle makes Lisbon-plus-Marrakesh one of the easiest two-city itineraries on the ACME Travel map. It is a no-frills 1h35m sector: carry-on included, checked bags and seat selection extra, snacks for purchase. Window seats on the left side get the Strait crossing on clear days.

specs.bag_allowance: 1 carry-on + personal item; checked 23 kg bag $25

review_highlights: Breakfast in Lisbon, lunch in the medina — still feels like a magic trick
Left side window for the Strait view, trust me
Budget hop, budget legroom, zero complaints at this price

products.title: New York to Marrakesh — Business, One Stop
products.short_description: Lie-flat across the Atlantic, lounge in Lisbon, and land in Marrakesh rested — fully refundable.
products.long_description: ACME Air Atlantic's business itinerary pairs a lie-flat suite on the overnight transatlantic leg with extra-legroom seating on the Marrakesh hop, plus lounge access at both ends of the Lisbon connection. The fare is fully refundable, changeable without fees, and includes two 32 kg bags and arrival transfer booking support. The flat bed on the long leg is what you are paying for, and it delivers.

specs.extras: lounges at origin and connection, priority everything

review_highlights: Slept flat, showered in the Lisbon lounge, arrived human
Every business seat has aisle access — no clambering
Worth it on the overnight outbound; we flew economy home

products.title: Los Angeles to Queenstown — Economy, One Stop
products.short_description: The overnight haul to Queenstown via Auckland — board at night, land in the Southern Alps the morning after next.
products.long_description: ACME Air Pacific's LA red-eye crosses the Pacific overnight, connects in Auckland, and descends into Queenstown's mountain bowl — widely considered one of the great approaches in commercial aviation, so fight for a window. The fare is non-refundable with one checked bag through-checked to Queenstown. You lose a day to the dateline going out and get it back coming home.

specs.entertainment: seatback screens on the long leg

review_highlights: The landing between the peaks is worth the whole trip
Long, but the overnight timing makes it survivable
Left window seats on the final leg for the mountain show

products.title: San Francisco to Queenstown — Premium Economy, One Stop
products.short_description: Premium economy for the long way south — refundable, two bags, and a ski-gear allowance built in.
products.long_description: Seventeen hours of travel is where premium economy stops being a luxury: ACME Air Pacific's cabin gives you 99 cm of pitch, a proper duvet for the overnight Pacific leg, and lounge access in Auckland. The refundable fare carries two checked bags plus one ski or snowboard bag free in winter season — a deliberate nod to the July-to-September Queenstown rush. Changes are free; only the fare difference applies.

specs.bag_allowance: 1 carry-on + 2 checked 23 kg bags + 1 ski bag (Jul-Sep)

review_highlights: The free ski bag quietly saved us $150 each way
Slept six hours over the Pacific — unheard of for me
Refundable matters when you're booking a ski trip months out

products.title: Auckland to Queenstown Nonstop — Economy
products.short_description: The scenic domestic hop down the spine of the South Island into Queenstown's mountain amphitheater.
products.long_description: ACME Air Pacific's midday Auckland-Queenstown rotation is the connector for travelers arriving on other carriers or spending a night up north first. The refundable fare includes a carry-on and free date changes; checked bags are a small add-on. On clear days the second half of the flight is an unbroken parade of braided rivers, lakes, and the Southern Alps — sit on the right going south.

specs.bag_allowance: 1 carry-on + personal item; checked 23 kg bag $18

review_highlights: Possibly the most scenic 110 minutes in domestic flying
Cheap, frequent, painless
Right-hand window southbound — thank me later

products.title: Alfama at Dusk: Fado & Petiscos Evening Walk
products.short_description: Wind through Alfama as the lamps come on, grazing on petiscos before ending at a live fado set in a family-run tavern.
products.long_description: ACME Tours' signature evening starts at a hilltop viewpoint at golden hour and descends through Alfama's tangle of lanes, stopping at three taverns for small plates and local wine. It ends seated at a tiny family-run fado house where the lights dim, talking stops, and someone's grandmother breaks your heart in two songs. Walking is gentle but cobbled — wear real shoes.

specs.includes: petiscos at 3 taverns, 2 glasses of wine, reserved fado seating
specs.meeting_point_type: public viewpoint, exact pin after booking

review_highlights: The fado finale had half our group in tears — no exaggeration
Felt like being shown around by a local friend with great taste
Eat a light lunch; the petiscos add up

products.title: Hands-On Azulejo Tile-Painting Workshop
products.short_description: Paint your own azulejo tile in a working Baixa atelier, guided by a ceramicist — fired, glazed, and shipped to you.
products.long_description: In a third-generation tile atelier off the Baixa grid, a working ceramicist walks you through the cobalt-on-white tradition before you sketch, trace, and paint your own 14 cm tile. Pieces are kiln-fired over the following week and shipped worldwide, included in the price. Beginner-proof and quietly addictive; many guests book a second session before leaving Lisbon.

specs.includes: all materials, apron, kiln firing, worldwide shipping of your tile
specs.meeting_point_type: studio, street address sent after booking

review_highlights: My wonky tile is now my favorite souvenir ever
The ceramicist's demo alone was worth the price
Tile arrived home in three weeks, beautifully packed

products.title: Sintra Palaces & Wild Coast Day Trip
products.short_description: A full day among Sintra's storybook palaces and gardens, ending with cliffs and salt spray on the wild Atlantic coast.
products.long_description: ACME Tours runs Sintra in reverse of the crowds: an early palace entry while the mist is still in the pines, a long garden wander, and a leisurely seafood lunch in a village the buses skip. The afternoon trades fairytale for drama — clifftop viewpoints on the Atlantic edge and the westernmost point of mainland Europe. Hotel pickup, entries, and lunch are all included.

specs.includes: hotel pickup, palace and garden entries, seafood lunch, coastal stops
specs.fitness_level: moderate — garden paths and short climbs

review_highlights: Beating the crowds into the palace changed everything
Lunch spot was the kind you could never find alone
Long day, completely full, completely worth it

products.title: Dawn Temple Walk & Tea Ceremony
products.short_description: Climb the Higashiyama temple paths at first light — before the city wakes — and end with a formal tea ceremony.
products.long_description: The flagship walk of ACME Tours meets at a temple gate at 6am, when the lanes of Higashiyama hold nothing but birdsong and the sound of monks sweeping gravel. A guide steeped in temple history leads two hours of walking and one unhurried hour of seated tea ceremony with a licensed tea master. Most guests call it the single best thing they did in Japan; the 6am start is the price of admission.

specs.includes: temple entry fees, full tea ceremony with sweets, guide
specs.meeting_point_type: temple gate, pin and photo sent after booking
specs.fitness_level: easy-moderate — 2 hours walking, some stone steps

review_highlights: Kyoto at 6am belongs to you — magic is the only word
The tea master explained everything without rushing anything
Set two alarms; you do not want to miss this one

products.title: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove & Riverside Cycling
products.short_description: Beat the crowds into the bamboo grove at opening, then spend the morning cycling the Katsura riverbank.
products.long_description: This half-day starts inside the bamboo grove minutes after it opens, while the light is still coming down in shafts and the paths are quiet. From there it becomes an easy-paced ride along the Katsura river — temples, monkeys on the far hillside, and a tea stop where the boats turn around. Bikes, helmets, and entries are included; the route is flat and unhurried.

specs.includes: bike and helmet, grove and temple entries, riverside tea stop
specs.fitness_level: easy — flat riverside cycling, 10 km total

review_highlights: Had the grove nearly to ourselves at 8am
The riverside ride was the sleeper highlight
Comfortable bikes, gentle pace, zero lycra required

products.title: Pontocho Evening Counter-Seat Food Crawl
products.short_description: Six seats, five counters, one lantern-lit alley — a guided eating tour of Pontocho's tiny bars and kitchens.
products.long_description: Pontocho's best food hides behind sliding doors with no English menus and five stools; the ACME Tours guide holds standing reservations at a rotating cast of them. Across three hours you'll eat five courses at five counters — yakitori, obanzai, seasonal surprises — with a sake flight woven through. Capped at six guests because that is what fits; non-refundable because the counters hold the seats either way.

specs.includes: 5 counter-seat tastings, sake flight, guide and all reservations

review_highlights: Doors we'd never have opened, food we still talk about
Six people max means you actually talk to the chefs
Come hungry and trust the guide's ordering

products.title: Markets of the Centro: Breakfast Crawl
products.short_description: Eat your way through two historic Centro markets — seven tastings from blue-corn quesadillas to café de olla.
products.long_description: The morning crawl of ACME Tours moves through two of the Centro's great covered markets while the vendors are still setting up for the day. Seven stops cover the canon — tamales from a steel pot, blue-corn quesadillas off the comal, fruit you cannot name yet, cinnamon-spiked café de olla — with the history of each market told between bites. Arrive hungry; leave incapacitated.

specs.includes: 7 tastings across 2 markets, fresh juice, café de olla
specs.meeting_point_type: market entrance, exact pin after booking

review_highlights: Seven stops in and every single one delivered
Our guide knew every vendor by name — that's the tour
Skip breakfast. This IS breakfast.

products.title: Xochimilco Trajinera Morning with Brunch
products.short_description: Drift the canals of Xochimilco on a private painted trajinera, with brunch aboard and the weekend chaos nowhere in sight.
products.long_description: ACME Tours runs Xochimilco on weekday mornings, when the canals belong to herons, chinampa farmers, and almost nobody else. Your group gets a private flower-painted trajinera, a brunch spread laid down the long table, and a guide who explains the floating-garden system that fed an empire. It is a different planet from the Saturday party flotilla — calmer, greener, and better photographed.

specs.includes: private trajinera, onboard brunch and agua fresca, canal-side farm stop
specs.fitness_level: none — you are on a boat

review_highlights: Weekday morning was the right call — silent, green, gorgeous
Brunch on the boat felt absurdly luxurious for the price
The chinampa farm stop was unexpectedly the best part

products.title: Masked Wrestling Night with a Superfan Host
products.short_description: Tacos, a cantina warm-up, then ringside-section seats for a night of high-flying masked wrestling.
products.long_description: Your host — a genuine lifelong superfan — starts the evening with street tacos and a cantina stop to teach you the chants, the heroes, and the villains worth booing. Then it's into the arena's lower section for two-plus hours of acrobatic mayhem, with your own souvenir mask included to wear immediately. Non-refundable because the tickets are real and the seats are good.

specs.includes: ringside-section ticket, taco stop, cantina drink, souvenir mask
specs.meeting_point_type: cantina near the arena, pin after booking
specs.fitness_level: none — but you will be on your feet cheering

review_highlights: Went in curious, left a lifelong fan, still own the mask
Our host's running commentary made the whole show
Loud, ridiculous, joyful — exactly as advertised

products.title: Geysers, Falls & Rift Valley 4x4 Day
products.short_description: Iceland's greatest hits in a six-seat 4x4 — erupting geysers, a thundering waterfall, and the rift between continents.
products.long_description: ACME Tours runs the classic circle in a lifted 4x4 that carries six, which means leaving on your schedule and detouring where the buses can't. The day covers the erupting geyser field, the double-cascade waterfall, and a walk through the rift valley where two tectonic plates pull slowly apart — plus a stop at a geothermal bakery for bread baked in the ground. Lunch and all entries included.

specs.includes: 4x4 transport, all entries, geothermal bakery tasting, lunch
specs.fitness_level: easy — short walks at each stop

review_highlights: Six people instead of sixty changes the entire day
Hot spring bread with Icelandic butter — core memory
Driver read the weather and flipped the route order; clever

products.title: Northern Lights Drive with a Photographer Guide
products.short_description: Chase the aurora with a guide who reads the forecasts for a living — tripods, thermal suits, and your photos included.
products.long_description: ACME Tours' aurora hunts leave town only when the data says go: cloud cover, solar wind, and a network of spotters decide the night's route. Guests get thermal suits, hot cocoa, mounted tripods, and a photographer-guide who shoots every guest under the lights — edited photos delivered within 48 hours. If the sky stays quiet, you rejoin free as many nights as it takes.

specs.includes: aurora-forecast routing, thermal suit, tripod, hot cocoa, edited photos
specs.fitness_level: none — short walks from the van

review_highlights: Struck out night one, rebooked free, night two was biblical
The photos they sent are framed on our wall
Thermal suits are not optional-feeling in November — bless them

products.title: Lava Fields Hike & Hot Spring Soak
products.short_description: Hike a young lava field on the Reykjanes peninsula, then soak it off in a steaming geothermal lagoon.
products.long_description: This half-day pairs the peninsula's rawest landscape — a moss-covered lava field with vents still breathing steam — with the reward of a long soak in a mineral-blue geothermal lagoon. The hike covers about six kilometers of uneven volcanic ground at an unhurried pace, with geology storytelling that makes recent eruptions feel very recent indeed. Lagoon entry and towel are included; bring a swimsuit and a sense of scale.

specs.includes: guided 6 km hike, lagoon entry, towel rental, transport from Reykjavik

review_highlights: Steam rising from the ground you're walking on — surreal
The soak afterward is perfectly engineered relief
Real hiking shoes, not sneakers; lava eats sneakers

products.title: Souks and Artisan Workshops Walk
products.short_description: Crack the code of the Marrakesh souks with a local guide — three artisan workshops, mint tea, and zero tourist traps.
products.long_description: ACME Tours' walk turns the souks from overwhelming to legible in three hours: through the dyers' lane, into a coppersmith's workshop, a weaving cooperative, and a wood-turner's stall barely wider than his lathe. Your guide explains what quality looks like, what fair prices sound like, and hands over a haggling cheat-sheet at the end. No commission stops, guaranteed in writing — guides are salaried, not kickbacked.

specs.includes: 3 artisan workshop visits, mint tea, haggling cheat-sheet
specs.meeting_point_type: landmark gate, exact pin after booking
specs.fitness_level: easy — 3 km of lanes at strolling pace

review_highlights: Went back alone the next day and actually knew where I was
The no-commission promise is real — zero pressure anywhere
Paid for itself with the first rug negotiation

products.title: Atlas Foothills Village Day with Home-Cooked Lunch
products.short_description: Trade the souk's noise for Atlas foothill villages, a valley walk among walnut groves, and tagine in a family home.
products.long_description: An hour south of Marrakesh the road climbs into Berber villages stacked up the hillsides, and the day slows to a walking pace: a guided valley trail through walnut and cherry groves, a working argan press, and a long lunch of tagine and fresh bread in a family's courtyard home. The drive back catches the High Atlas in late-afternoon light. Hotel pickup, the walk, and lunch are all included.

specs.includes: 4x4 transport with hotel pickup, guided valley walk, home-cooked tagine lunch
specs.fitness_level: moderate — 5 km valley walk, gentle grades

review_highlights: Lunch in that courtyard was the best meal of the entire trip
The mountains feel a world away from the medina — go
Our host's grandmother taught us to fold msemen; no notes

products.title: Alpine Sunrise Hike & Backcountry Breakfast
products.short_description: Climb by headlamp to a ridgeline above Queenstown, watch dawn hit the lake, then eat a hot cooked breakfast at altitude.
products.long_description: The sunrise hike of ACME Tours leaves town in the dark and gains the ridge just as the first light slides down the ranges and onto Lake Wakatipu — a view you'll have nearly alone. Guides then unpack a genuinely hot breakfast: eggs, sausages, flat whites from a backcountry press. The route gains 450 meters at a steady, supported pace; headlamps and trekking poles are provided. Runs spring onward as snow clears the trail.

specs.includes: guide, headlamps, trekking poles, hot cooked breakfast, summit coffee

review_highlights: Watching dawn pour down the ranges with coffee in hand — top five life moments
Hard enough to earn it, supported enough to finish it
The breakfast is not a granola bar. It is BREAKFAST.

products.title: Lake Wakatipu Evening Cruise & Stargazing
products.short_description: Glide out onto Lake Wakatipu at dusk with mulled wine, then cut the engines for guided southern-sky stargazing.
products.long_description: The twilight cruise motors out as the ranges go pink, serves mulled wine as the light dies, and then shuts everything down — engines, lights, chatter — in the middle of the lake under some of the darkest accessible skies in the southern hemisphere. A guide with a laser pointer and two telescopes walks you through the Southern Cross, the galactic core, and whatever the season is showing off. Winter sailings sell out weeks ahead; dress like you mean it.

specs.includes: 2.5 h cruise, mulled wine, blankets, telescope stargazing session

review_highlights: The moment they cut the lights, the sky simply detonated
Mulled wine + blankets + southern stars = perfect evening
Book early in winter; we nearly missed out
